findings.issue: Asymmetric exception handling: OnAfterRenderAsync (line 210) now correctly catches `JSException or JSDisconnectedException or ObjectDisposedException`, but OnDateInputAsync's getSelectionStart call (line 168) still catches only `JSException`. JSDisconnectedException/ObjectDisposedException do not derive from JSException, so a keystroke whose interop round-trip races window/renderer teardown throws out of the event handler; an unhandled exception in a Blazor event handler tears the renderer down exactly as one from a lifecycle method does, which is the same failure the OnAfterRenderAsync widening was made to prevent.
findings.fix: In OnDateInputAsync change `catch (JSException)` to `catch (Exception ex) when (ex is JSException or JSDisconnectedException or ObjectDisposedException)`, keeping the existing `caret = raw.Length;` fallback body.

findings.issue: The new `_inputSeq` out-of-order guard (WInput.razor lines 71, 157, 173-178) is the only behavioural change of the fix2 round with no test at all: deleting the `if (seq != _inputSeq) { return; }` block keeps all of this package's 25 tests green. The guard also silently suppresses ValueChanged for a superseded keystroke, a behaviour nothing pins down.
findings.fix: Add a bUnit fact that makes the interop round-trip observable-ordered — e.g. stub `wakeelUi.getSelectionStart` with a planned/deferred result (JSInterop.Setup<int>(...) whose SetResult is invoked after the second Input() call), issue two Input() calls, then assert that only the newer keystroke's (value, caret) pair reaches `wakeelUi.setInputValue` and that the recorded ValueChanged sequence ends on the newer value.

MASKED-DATE EDGE CASES (bUnit verified; the manual host check was blocked by finding 1, and was verified live in the previous round). Null initial value: first and second rejected keystrokes both reach setInputValue with ("",0) and ("1",1) — the case the old guard got wrong. Rejected character after two digits: value stays "12", DOM corrected with caret after the last accepted digit, not at the end of the rejected text. Middle insertion: "12/09" + "5" at index 3 -> "12/50/9" with caret 4, i.e. beside the inserted digit. Arabic-indic digits are normalised to Western (ARCHITECTURE.md §12) and non-digits dropped; FormatDateMask truncates past 8 digits; CountDigitsBefore clamps the caret with Math.Min against raw.Length, so an out-of-range selectionStart cannot throw.

SECURITY — CLEAN. `getSelectionStart(el)` reads only `el.selectionStart` on the element reference it is handed and type-checks it; `setInputValue(el, value, caret)` null-checks, assigns `el.value` and clamps the caret with Math.max/Math.min before setSelectionRange. Neither takes a selector, an id, or any string that is evaluated: no eval, no innerHTML, no document-wide query, and no path to any element other than the `_dateRef` ElementReference the component owns. Removing setCaretPosition shrank the interop surface. The password field uses the plain OnInputAsync path and never touches either helper, so no password, key or seed reaches JS, the log, the database or lingering UI state.
